hints.title: Separating Directions
hints.text: A consecutive subarray either has common adjacent difference +1 (strictly increasing) or -1 (strictly decreasing).

hints.title: Contribution Technique
hints.text: For a contiguous run of length L with step diff, maintain the running sum of all ending subarrays at index i by multiplying each incoming element by its count of extensions.

hints.title: Inclusion-Exclusion on Singletons
hints.text: Subarrays of length 1 are consecutive under both difference +1 and difference -1 definitions. Subtract the sum of all individual elements to avoid double counting.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def getSum(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        MOD = 1_000_000_007
        n = len(nums)
        if n == 0:
            return 0
            
        def sum_consecutive(diff: int) -> int:
            total = 0
            curr_sum = nums[0]
            curr_cnt = 1
            total = (total + curr_sum) % MOD
            
            for i in range(1, n):
                if nums[i] - nums[i - 1] == diff:
                    curr_sum = (curr_sum + nums[i] * (curr_cnt + 1)) % MOD
                    curr_cnt += 1
                else:
                    curr_sum = nums[i]
                    curr_cnt = 1
                total = (total + curr_sum) % MOD
            return total
            
        inc_sum = sum_consecutive(1)
        dec_sum = sum_consecutive(-1)
        single_elements_sum = sum(nums) % MOD
        
        # Single element subarrays were counted in both inc_sum and dec_sum
        return (inc_sum + dec_sum - single_elements_sum) % MOD
```

complexity.notes: Two linear scans compute increasing and decreasing run sums in O(n) total time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating all O(n^2) subarrays directly leads to TLE on large arrays.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Maintains running totals in O(1) auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Decomposes the condition into increasing and decreasing passes and avoids double-counting single elements.
